objective: Verify the DR24 Explorer browser view against the live FastAPI-to-HATS route for three OIDs. Confirm that the chart, raw table, provenance, and quality-flag highlighting match the independently verified payloads.
previous_knowledge_consumed: PR #267 adds a separate DR24 Explorer view that calls the raw DR24 API route and does not run inference.
PR #270 verified the FastAPI route against live HATS for three OIDs; all API payload hashes matched the independent probe artifact.
The expected OID epoch counts are 78, 123, and 216.
The expected bit-15 catflags counts are 7, 8, and 25; flagged epochs must remain visible.
The Workbench renders at most 50 epoch rows and plots all finite epochs.

baseline.description: This is a browser test branch stacked on PR #267, which is itself stacked on PR #264. No default-branch, model, feature, taxonomy, benchmark, or release changes.

correctness.before: The DR24 Explorer UI had not been tested against live HATS data.
correctness.after: Workflow 42064925261 passed on code revision 29f7b23396efdfc6b6dbea97994de4532e58f15c. Chromium rendered 78, 123, and 216 chart points for three OIDs. All three displayed payload hashes matched the independent HATS reference.

reproducibility.after: Artifact 13433621371 was uploaded. ZIP SHA-256: ba28da858620dbeb0b8fcbe7ca177f2723f582c9ceef1d4e0ab61d15bdeb6844. The JSON report records the code revision, workflow run, OIDs, epoch counts, chart points, quality-flag counts, and hashes.

reliability.before: The UI had no live-browser integration result.
reliability.after: The browser test passed for all three OIDs. It verified the loading and response states, provenance source, 50-row table rendering, chart point counts, and flagged/unflagged point counts.

scientific_validity.reason: The browser view displays raw data only. It does not validate astrophysical identity, features, inference, calibration, OOD, or anomaly performance.

measurement.trade_off: Use a browser-only test with three previously verified OIDs. Install Playwright only in the dedicated workflow; do not add it to runtime dependencies.

evidence: The test starts the real FastAPI application with the real DR24LightcurveBackend.
The test uses Chromium and the actual Workbench static assets from PR #267.
The test compares displayed payload hashes with the independent HATS probe references.
The test checks chart point counts, flagged/unflagged point counts, 50-row table rendering, and provenance.
The test is skipped in ordinary offline CI unless ZTF_DR24_WORKBENCH_LIVE_TEST=1 is set.
The branch-scoped workflow installs Playwright and uploads only a compact JSON evidence artifact.

unresolved: The passing browser test used code revision 29f7b23396efdfc6b6dbea97994de4532e58f15c. Re-run against the current PR head after the lifecycle record update.
Test the no-record UI state and source-failure UI state.
A 5–10 object end-to-end application smoke test with QC, exports, and a reproducibility bundle remains open.

findings: API payload parity does not by itself prove that the Workbench renders the correct data.
Chart point counts and flagged-point colors can be checked against raw catflags without filtering epochs.
The browser test must use the same API endpoint and independent payload hashes as the API smoke test.

open_blockers: Re-run the live browser test against the latest PR head.
Test the no-record UI state and source-failure UI state.
Complete a 5–10 object application smoke test before the 30–50 object Park demonstration.

knowledge_carried_forward: Do not claim Workbench UI validation until the browser workflow passes.
Keep the DR24 Explorer raw-only and separate from the frozen v0.2.0 inference contract.
Do not filter catflags or relabel HMJD.
Do not claim Park MVP acceptance from this three-OID browser smoke test.
